comments.body:
Root cause confirmed on origin/main 82a91a89f1d, no LLM.

- In-process: begin_gate_job("verify_completion", T, variant="graph=None;source=attested"), edit_ticket(T), begin_gate_job again -> is_new=False and the same job id, while show_ticket already returned the edited text.
- Tool-level red (tests/unit/test_mcp_llm_dedup.py): verify_completion_start after an edit returned the same job id; sync verify_completion ran the gate once instead of twice. Both pass with the fix.
- Raising read: the key-shape test makes current_material_fingerprint raise. On 82a91a89f1d the plan-review variant (3040's _plan_review_variant) lets it escape, which fails the tool call before the gate starts. The shared _material_key now degrades it to material=None for both variants.
- Existing tests: test_two_concurrent_calls_invoke_the_gate_exactly_once[verify_completion] passes unchanged. test_verify_completion_start_preserves_graph_tristate_and_variant_key pinned the literal old variant; its start/sync parity and graph=None assertions are unchanged, and only the literal gained ";material=None". File impact and plan updated for that; plan re-review running.

Signing defect found while scoping this: daredevil-marginal-dodo (0521-7e68). The attached pre-edit run signs post-edit material, and a close reuses it. That defect is not fixed by this change.

compiled_state.description:
## Problem

The MCP gate singleflight key (`src/rebar/_mcp_inflight.py` `compute_key`) hashes gate,
canonical ticket id, code basis SHA, variant, and readonly flag. Both completion call sites in
`src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py` pass `variant=f"graph={graph};source={source or 'attested'}"`:
`verify_completion_start` (~line 313) and the sync `verify_completion` tool (~line 420). The
ticket's text is not in the key. So while a completion check of ticket T is in flight, editing T
and starting another check returns the SAME run, which read the old text when it started.

This is the same mechanism fixed for plan review in next-embattled-geese (3b27-8f4b, Gerrit
3040), which added the material fingerprint via `_plan_review_variant`.

Harm is worse than for plan review. Plan review re-checks its material under the store lock
before signing; completion does not (bug daredevil-marginal-dodo, 0521-7e68). The attached
pre-edit run signs a PASS whose manifest binds the POST-edit material, and a close then reuses
it. Dedup therefore routes the author's correct "edit, then re-verify" into that hole: they
receive a signed PASS for text that was never verified. This ticket stops the re-verify from
attaching; daredevil-marginal-dodo fixes what the attached run signs. Both are needed; this one
does not depend on the other.

## Plan

1. Add `_completion_variant(ticket_id, graph, source)` in `src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py` returning
   `f"graph={graph};source={source or 'attested'};material={fp}"`, with `fp` from
   `rebar.llm.plan_review.attest.current_material_fingerprint(ticket_id)` (light read, no LLM).
2. Use it at both completion call sites. In `verify_completion_start` compute it inside the
   worker thread (same as `review_plan_start`), not on the event loop.
3. `material=None` arm: `current_material_fingerprint_impl` returns None on a read failure,
   and RE-RAISES a pinned ticket-view failure. A shared `_material_key` catches a raising read
   and returns None, so a gate start never fails on its own dedup key; the gate still runs and
   reports the read failure. `_plan_review_variant` (3040) uses the same helper: on
   82a91a89f1d a raising read escapes it and fails the tool call before the gate starts. None
   keys dedup only with each other, never with a run keyed on a real fingerprint.
4. `tests/unit/test_mcp_gate_async.py::test_verify_completion_start_preserves_graph_tristate_and_variant_key`
   pins the literal old variant `graph=None;source=attested`. Its purpose (graph tri-state kept,
   start and sync share one key) is unchanged; only the expected literal gains
   `;material=None` (its ticket `d80d` does not exist in that store, so the read returns None).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Test in `tests/unit/test_mcp_llm_dedup.py`: a blocked `verify_completion_start` run is in
  flight, the description is edited, a second start returns a NEW job whose gate call sees the
  edited text. Fails on origin/main 82a91a89f1d.
- [ ] Same through the sync `verify_completion` tool: after an edit, a concurrent call runs the
  gate a second time. Fails on origin/main.
- [ ] Unchanged material still dedups: the existing
  `test_two_concurrent_calls_invoke_the_gate_exactly_once[verify_completion]` passes unchanged.
- [ ] Key-shape test, for both the completion and plan-review variants: different fingerprints
  give different variants; a None fingerprint AND a raising read both give the
  `...;material=None` variant, distinct from both. The raising-read case fails on 82a91a89f1d.
- [ ] The graph tri-state test still asserts start/sync key parity, with the updated literal.

## Testing
```
.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_mcp_llm_dedup.py tests/unit/test_mcp_inflight.py tests/unit/test_mcp_gate_async.py -p no:randomly -q
make lint && make typecheck && make verify
```

file_impact.reason: completion dedup variant at verify_completion_start and sync verify_completion includes the current plan-material fingerprint, computed in the worker thread; shared _material_key degrades a raising read to material=None for both gate variants
regression oracle: edit while a completion check is in flight gets a fresh run; unchanged material still dedups; key-shape test incl. None and raising reads
graph tri-state test pins the literal variant; expected literal gains ;material=None
